title: MaxKB code sandbox -- T1036 frame-introspected UUID forges tool-execution result via fd 1
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-39419 (GHSA-f3c8-p474-xwfv), a
self-reported advisory for MaxKB, affecting versions 2.7.1 and below.

MaxKB's sandbox wrapper embeds a per-execution UUID (as a bytecode
constant) that it prefixes to its legitimate result line, so the host
service can identify which line in mixed stdout is the genuine tool
result. An authenticated user can defeat this: using
`sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_consts` (Python frame introspection), code
running inside the sandbox reads the wrapper's own compiled bytecode
constants to recover that UUID at runtime -- a value that was never
meant to be readable from inside the sandboxed code. It then writes a
FORGED result line, carrying the same UUID prefix, directly to file
descriptor 1 via `os.write` -- bypassing any stdout redirection the
wrapper itself might otherwise rely on -- and calls `sys.exit(0)` to
terminate the wrapper before it ever emits its own legitimate output.
The host service, which trusts the LAST line matching the UUID prefix,
parses and acts on the attacker's forged result as if it were genuine.

Detection logic flags the structural pattern this bypass depends on:
a sandboxed process whose captured output shows a `sys.exit(0)` call
occurring immediately after a raw `os.write` to file descriptor 1 --
the specific write-then-exit sequence that lets a forged line become
the wrapper's apparent final output.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (1Panel-dev, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 2.8.0.
